comments.body: Shipped as part of e3153393 - len rode along with the constraint enforcement work, sharing every layer it touches.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Falls out of the model settled in `collect-bare`: `targets str[]` means "at least one value", `targets str[] = []` means "may be empty". That rule is real but a script can't state it, and can't ask for anything else.

`len` would make it sayable, reusing the interval notation `range` already uses:

```rad
args:
    pair str[] len [2,2]      // exactly two
    sample len [3,5)          // three or four
    *ports int len [1,]       // at least one
```

leaving `targets str[]` and `targets str[] = []` as the implicit `[1,]` and `[0,]` cases.

Wanted for `str[]`/`int[]`/`float[]`/`bool[]` and `*name`. Should render in usage and in the validation error the way `range` does - scalar `range` prints `Range: [0, 100]` in the args block and fails with `'score' value 500 is > maximum 100`.

A new constraint keyword means a `tree-sitter-rad` grammar rule alongside the existing `arg_enum_constraint` / `arg_regex_constraint` / `arg_range_constraint`, so this reaches grammar, converter, `ra` and usage rendering rather than being a Rad-only change.

Pairs with `scalar-arg`: `len` bounds how many values, the scalar constraints bound each one.
title: Add a len constraint for list and variadic args
